# KnowBridge — Round 2 report

**Team:** Fallen Crows · **Stage:** Round 2 — The Build
**Product:** AI-assisted knowledge handover, documents-only build
**Repository:** this repository · **Demo data:** `demo-data/documents/` (synthetic, generated by
`scripts/gen_demo_docs.py`)

---

## 1. What a judge can do with this build

The central workflow runs end to end without a manual step being simulated:

| Step | Where | What happens |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1. Connect | Sources tab | Manager uploads PDF, DOCX, TXT or MD; text is extracted and chunked with headings preserved |
| 2. Reconstruct | Run AI extraction | Groq returns atomic claims; each is classified into one of ten categories and mapped to a handover section |
| 3. Verify | Map / Claims | Every claim shows its document, section and verbatim quote; status is `supported`, `needs_review`, `conflicting` or `unsupported`; contradictions between documents and decisions with no named owner are surfaced |
| 4. Review | Claims / Handover | Manager or reviewer verifies, corrects, redacts or excludes claims, adds a reviewer note, then approves |
| 5. Hand over | Handover version → recipient view | The incoming person signs in and receives only the sections their role allows; redacted claims never appear; opening and acknowledgement are audited |

Try it with the seeded accounts (`npm run seed`): `manager@knowbridge.demo` and
`incoming@knowbridge.demo`, password `KnowBridge2026!`.

## 3. How the evidence model works

A model output is never stored as fact on its own authority:

1. The model must return an **exact quote** from the passage it read.
2. The server normalises and searches that quote inside the passage. Missing quote → `unsupported`;
   quote not found → `needs_review`; found → `supported`.
3. Claim text, original model text, quote, document, section, extraction time and reviewer are all
   stored separately, so a correction never destroys the audit basis.
4. Approval snapshots only non-excluded claims. Recipients read the snapshot, not live data, so
   later edits cannot change an approved handover.

Contradictions are detected without a model: two claims with opposing status words (`pending` vs
`complete`, `disabled` vs `active`, `blocked` vs `resolved`) and at least 40 % subject overlap from
different passages are both marked `conflicting`. The system displays both and asks the reviewer to
decide. It deliberately does not arbitrate.

## 4. Changes from the Round 1 plan, and why

| Change | Reason |
| --- | --- |
| **GitHub connector removed; documents only** | The central workflow had to be reliable for a judge with one sitting. Keeping one ingestion path let the build spend its time on evidence checking, conflict detection and permission scoping instead of a second credential-dependent integration. The document pipeline is where the traceability claim is demonstrated; the connector is the first Round 3 commitment. |
| **Gemini mentioned in §3.2 → Groq** | The §3.1 stack table already specified Groq and the API key was available. One line of §3.2 was inaccurate; this note corrects it. |
| **Mobile app deferred** | §5.2 allowed responsive web first. The web build is responsive; the recipient view is usable on a phone. |
| **No per-table RLS policies for users** | All access goes through the Express API with the service-role key and explicit membership checks. RLS is enabled with no public policies, so the browser cannot read tables directly even with an anon key. Policies for direct-client access are not needed by this architecture. |
| **Reviewer edits claims, not a copy** | One source of truth during review. The snapshot exists only to freeze what was shared. |

## 5. Technical depth and reliability

- **Permission model with two layers.** The API resolves the bearer token (`auth.getUser`), then
  checks project membership. Membership guards always include the auth guard, so a route cannot be
  protected by membership alone. Recipient scope is read from `project_members`; query parameters
  are ignored, so a recipient cannot request a wider view.
- **Failure isolation.** One unreadable document does not fail the upload batch; one failed passage
  does not fail the extraction run. Failures are reported in the UI and the run summary.
- **Rate-limit handling.** Groq calls retry with backoff on 429/5xx, three concurrent passages at a
  time.
- **Bounded data handling.** Files are parsed in memory, stored as text chunks only, and removing a
  source cascades to its claims. Binary uploads are never persisted.
- **Deterministic core.** Permissions, evidence checks, conflicts and scoping are plain code; the
  model is confined to turning passages into candidate claims.

No other third-party services, datasets or templates are used. Demo content is synthetic.

## 7. Verification

Executed against the seeded Ledgerline demo project.

**Automated**

- `npm run typecheck` passes for `shared`, `server` and `web`.
- `npm run build -w web` produces a 180 kB bundle (55 kB gzipped).
- API smoke test: `/healthz` responds; unauthenticated `GET /api/projects` → 401; invalid
  credentials → 401.

**End to end**

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Upload 6 documents (MD, TXT, DOCX, PDF) | 6 sources `ready`, 13 passages |
| Extraction | 67 claims: 64 `supported`, 1 `needs_review`, 2 `conflicting`, 0 `unsupported`, 4 ownership gaps |
| Planted contradiction | detected: "retry queue not yet deployed" (runbook) vs "deployed and live" (status update) |
| Review actions | 2 claims verified, 1 excluded, 1 redacted; each recorded with reviewer and timestamp |
| Approval | v1 approved and frozen with 66 claims; previous approved versions superseded |
| Recipient view (scope `engineer`) | 65 claims across 9 sections; excluded and redacted claims absent; reviewer note shown |
| Escalation attempt | `?role=manager` ignored — scope still `engineer` |
| Scope change to `general` | view falls to overview, pending, next actions: 24 claims, 42 withheld; restoring `engineer` restores the view |
| Acknowledgement | recorded once per user and returned in the recipient payload |
| Audit | project creation, source adds, extraction, claim corrections, draft, approval, handover openings (with scope) and acknowledgement all present |

**Defects found and fixed during verification**

1. `PATCH /api/claims/:id` resolved the profile without running the auth guard, so every reviewer
   correction returned 500. The route now composes `requireAuth`.
2. `pdf-parse` bundles pdf.js 1.10 and could not read a modern PDF (`bad XRef entry`). Replaced with
   `pdfjs-dist`, which parses the same file correctly.
3. The configured Groq model was not available on this account, and a fatal 404 was retried for
   minutes. The model was switched to one the key can use and non-retryable errors now fail at once.
4. A 8k-token-per-minute limit aborted long runs. Retries now honour Groq's `retry after` hint, and
   extraction is incremental: passages that already produced claims are skipped, so a rate-limited
   run can simply be repeated.

## 8. Three improvements committed for Round 3

1. **A second source type with cross-source synthesis.** Add a read-only GitHub connector
   (README, issues, recent commits) and merge those claims with document claims into one timeline
   with per-source evidence, so a judge can see the same claim supported by a document and an
   issue.

2. **Review-preserving re-extraction and version comparison.** Re-running extraction will map new
   claims onto previous reviewer decisions (verified, corrected, redacted) instead of resetting
   them, and the handover will show a diff between approved versions plus rollback, so a handover
   can be refreshed as the project changes without losing human judgement.

3. **Confidentiality tiers and delivered handover.** Introduce per-source confidentiality, enforced
   in the scoping layer so a restricted document can never appear in any recipient view, and
   deliver handovers through expiring signed links with acknowledgement reminders — the delivery
   and access half of the problem, not just the generation half.

## 9. Known limitations

- Categorisation quality depends on the model; the same passage can produce slightly different
  claims between runs.
- Conflict detection is conservative: it misses contradictions that do not use opposing status
  words.
- No date extraction or cross-document timeline yet.
- Single-manager approval; no separation of reviewer and approver beyond the role model.
- Recipient links are hash routes shared manually; there is no email delivery.
- Groq's tokens-per-minute ceiling means a large document set may need a second extraction run; the
  run summary reports every passage that did not complete, and the next run picks it up.
